title: Pick the right vendor for the task
summary: Pick software for a function given YOUR context: define requirements, research and shortlist the market, compare candidates on judged evidence against the stack you already run, trial the finalists agentically, then security review, negotiation, and a signed agreement. Rollout hands off to the Connect a vendor or MCP server process.
outcomes: A buying brief and source-linked comparison that distinguishes satisfied, failed and unknown requirements.
A reproducible trial record with outputs, failures, manual interventions and plan/access limits.
A purchasing decision or explicit unresolved decision, with any contracting and rollout work reported separately.
guidance: Agree whether this run ends with a purchasing decision or includes already authorized contracting and rollout. Reuse the company buying brief and existing stack before asking for new facts. A decision-ready result contains requirement-level evidence, trial outputs, costs and unresolved questions; it may recommend retaining the incumbent or selecting no candidate. Mark unrun trials and unavailable access explicitly. A selected vendor is not contracted or installed until the corresponding agreement and rollout evidence exist. Keep the exact approved scope and remaining owner actions with the decision.

parts.title: Define requirements and constraints
parts.guidance:
Describe the job the company needs the software to perform, who will use it, and the current tools or manual process it would replace. Gather budget, expected usage, integration, export, security, and data-location requirements from their owners. Separate essential constraints from preferences and define how a successful trial will be judged. Record agreed priorities and flag unresolved tradeoffs for the purchasing owner; reversible desk research can proceed while those choices remain open.

Name the purchasing owner and record each essential requirement with its acceptance check. Include the incumbent and the cost of changing workflows. Establish the data and permission scope allowed for trials; absent trial access is a constraint, not evidence that the product fails.

For a formation, tax or other regulated service, include the relevant jurisdiction, entity type, service scope and deadline in the brief. Check provider eligibility and exclusions from current evidence or a qualified reviewer. Unresolved coverage becomes a disqualifier or question for the provider; a vendor listing or attractive price does not resolve it.

Before broad market research, save a compact buying brief and an evidence matrix with one row per essential requirement. Mark unverified entries unknown. Keep these artifacts usable even if the run pauses before a recommendation; a conversation-only plan does not preserve the working comparison.

execution.rationale: The authored work for “Define requirements and constraints” is preparation, analysis or editing of supplied records with text, file or code tools. Any named human decisions and subsequent external actions retain their existing gates.

parts.title: Research the market and shortlist
parts.guidance:
Search the market against the current buying brief, starting with current product documentation, pricing, and support information. Include relevant tools the company already owns and record why each candidate enters or leaves the shortlist. Verify consequential claims with direct documentation or a trial, distinguishing unavailable facts from negative findings. Present the purchasing owner with a manageable set of candidates, source links and checked dates, and the questions that need vendor clarification before comparison.

Update the saved evidence matrix as sources are checked, retaining candidate, plan, link, date and unresolved verification. Bound repeated searches that no longer resolve the decision: save the current tradeoffs and the exact remaining checks, with a provisional or trial-only recommendation where necessary. Do not turn an unknown price, relationship or export capability into a passed requirement to finish the shortlist.

execution.rationale: The supported path for “Research the market and shortlist” is a person working through the stated digital records, service or communication channel. Retain the named owners, approvals and expert review. This classification does not claim a verified agent integration or imply that future automation is impossible.

parts.title: Compare on evidence and rank against your stack
parts.guidance:
Compare candidates against the buying brief using current evidence, proposed plans, and the integrations the company needs. Show strengths, missing requirements, switching effort, and expected cost. Keep unknowns distinguishable from failed requirements. If using scores, make the criteria and calculations reproducible without altering published vendor rankings. Recommend a shortlist with the important tradeoffs, then turn consequential uncertainties into trial tasks or focused questions for the vendor.

Retain a comparison row for every essential requirement, identifying the candidate, plan, evidence location and observation date. Use unknown when a consequential fact is missing. Where plausible alternatives exist, compare more than one against the same task; do not manufacture alternatives to fill a table.

Calculate cost over the company’s decision horizon using actual seats/usage, mandatory feature add-ons, migration effort, minimum commitments and renewal terms. Distinguish monthly billing from a monthly cancellation right. When a corrected quote or retest changes the recommendation, update the comparison, recommendation and handoff together; retain previous evidence with its superseded scope. A cheaper option that fails an essential requirement remains ineligible.

notes.text: Start with UM's arena stories and requirement-level verdicts, then follow their evidenceIds to dated evidence. Match the company's job, plan, constraints and incumbent before interpreting an overall rank. The CRM openness-full-export verdict for HubSpot, for example, records gaps in complete export coverage; its contacts API evidence cannot establish a restorable company archive. A verdict's missing evidence becomes a focused trial or provider question, not a claim that the product lacks the feature. Keep documentation claims, recorded probes and completed task trials distinct. Refresh consequential price, eligibility and capability facts from primary sources and preserve the UM evidence that changed the decision.

references.title: UM CRM requirement-level verdicts
references.description: CRM verdicts expose requirement-level evidence gaps, including full export, that can become focused trial questions.

references.title: Evidence behind the HubSpot comparison
references.description: Dated HubSpot source entries let the reader trace a CRM verdict to its documentation or recorded probe.

execution.rationale: The authored work for “Compare on evidence and rank against your stack” is preparation, analysis or editing of supplied records with text, file or code tools. Any named human decisions and subsequent external actions retain their existing gates.

parts.title: Trial top candidates agentically
parts.guidance:
Turn the essential requirements into representative tasks with observable acceptance checks. Set up trial accounts using data cleared for that service, with approval for charges, sensitive access, or external actions. Have the agent perform the tasks through the available interface and inspect the outputs, including failures and manual intervention. Compare results across candidates and note plan limits or missing features that would change the purchase decision.

Save the exact trial input, interface and environment, operation attempted, expected result and observed artifact for each candidate. Include a relevant failure or recovery case, such as a truncated export or lost response, and check a recovered artifact for missing records and relationships. A successful API call or screenshot alone does not establish that the task worked. Stop before new grants, charges or external effects outside the trial authority. An unavailable trial remains untested; retain the prepared test for the owner.

Begin with synthetic data and minimum access. Complete the relevant data review before introducing sensitive company data, even if the full security review is scheduled later. For a write-capable workflow, test an allowed operation, denied out-of-scope access, and a retry or recovery that could duplicate or lose work. Preserve negative findings; a later passing test supersedes only the behavior and configuration it actually retested. Update the final recommendation from the trial findings and commercial/security review. A failed essential requirement must change eligibility or remain an explicit unresolved condition; a pre-trial ranking is not the final decision.

execution.rationale: The actual work and delivery method for “Trial top candidates agentically” depend on the selected service, product or trial. That choice can change the actor and medium. Keep the assessment unresolved until the concrete method is known rather than infer an agent capability from the vendor list.

parts.title: Security and data review
parts.guidance: Give security and privacy reviewers the intended data flows, permissions, vendor responses, and relevant assessment reports. Examine retention, deletion, access administration, subprocessors, and incident handling for this specific use. Resolve missing evidence with the vendor and record any required configuration or contractual condition. The designated reviewers decide whether the proposed use can proceed, needs changes, or is unsuitable before sensitive company data or a binding contract commits the business.

execution.rationale: The documented “Security and data review” work uses digital records, an online service or a remote communication channel and retains its named human owner. Agent assistance does not transfer the human decision, identity or signing responsibility.

parts.title: Negotiate pricing and terms
parts.guidance: Use expected usage, trial results, budget, and security conditions to set a negotiation position. Compare the whole commercial proposal, including plan limits, renewal, price changes, support, and exit or migration terms. Negotiate within the purchasing owner's mandate and take legal terms to counsel. Keep concessions and unresolved points in the proposal, then obtain approval for the final total commitment and material exceptions before preparing the signature package.

execution.rationale: “Negotiate pricing and terms” requires human participation or judgment. The retained work does not choose a remote/digital conversation or physical presence, so the Human Online versus Human Offline distinction remains open. Preserve the human owner and choose the actual medium.

parts.title: Prepare the agreement for signature
parts.guidance: Assemble the final order form, agreement, and applicable data-protection or security schedules. Check entities, prices, dates, renewal terms, and negotiated changes across the package, including attachments incorporated by reference. Resolve inconsistencies with the purchasing and legal owners before they clear the signing version. Identify the authorized signer and verified recipients, then prepare the signature request with that exact package and any conditions still required for execution.

execution.rationale: The authored work for “Prepare the agreement for signature” is preparation, analysis or editing of supplied records with text, file or code tools. Any named human decisions and subsequent external actions retain their existing gates.

parts.title: Sign the agreement
parts.guidance: Present the final package to the authorized company signer with the financial commitment, renewal terms, and accepted exceptions identified. Confirm that the attachments match the reviewed version, then complete execution through the agreed method and obtain the fully signed agreement. Give billing, renewal, and service obligations to their operational owners, using the effective terms to determine when account activation and rollout can begin.

execution.rationale: The documented “Sign the agreement” work uses digital records, an online service or a remote communication channel and retains its named human owner. Agent assistance does not transfer the human decision, identity or signing responsibility.

parts.title: Connect and roll out to the team
parts.guidance:
Plan the rollout around a small initial user group, necessary integrations, data migration, training, and the tasks users must be able to complete. Use the connection process for native integrations or MCP servers and arrange the required access with their owners. Try a representative workflow with the initial users, fix blockers, then expand access. Agree when the old workflow can be retired and who handles support or migration problems during the transition.

Verify the initial users can complete the agreed business task with the intended account and access. Retain the resulting record or artifact and unresolved rollout issues. Until that check passes, keep the old workflow available and report the handoff as pending rather than calling the purchase operational.

execution.rationale: The actual work and delivery method for “Connect and roll out to the team” depend on the selected service, product or trial. That choice can change the actor and medium. Keep the assessment unresolved until the concrete method is known rather than infer an agent capability from the vendor list.

metadata.supportReason: Requirements, market research, evidence comparison, and agentic trials run end-to-end; the security review, negotiation judgment, and the countersigned agreement stay human.
